Digimon World 2 Online Tools

Info on these pages comes from the original Digimon World 2 (PS1), plus the balance changes and info from DW2 Online. I’ll keep updating it as things change.

DNA Digivolve
  • Parents to result: enter two Champion, Ultimate or Mega Digimon to see what they make. To see everything one Digimon can make, enter just that one and press Possible combos.
  • Find combos: enter the Digimon you want in Result name, then open it to see every pair of parents that makes it. Use Parent includes to show only combos that use a certain Digimon.
  • Reading combos: each combo has a group of Digimon on each side of the +. Any Digimon from the left plus any from the right gives the same result.
  • Result stage: the result is one stage below the parents. Two Champions make a Rookie, two Ultimates make a Champion and two Megas make an Ultimate.

Parent includes
 

Parents at different levels: the higher parent is first brought down to the lower one’s level, as if it were DNA Digivolved with itself. The result then comes from the two same-level Digimon. Example: Apemon (Champion) + Etemon (Ultimate). Etemon + Etemon = Ogremon (Champion), so Apemon + Etemon gives the same result as Apemon + Ogremon, which is Tapirmon.

Mutations are special results that break the normal pattern:

  • M-Tyrannomon, MetalGreymon, Whamon or Zudomon + Cherrymon = Vademon
  • H-Kabuterimon + Baihumon, M-Garurumon, P-Mamemon or SaberLeomon = SandYanmamon
  • H-Kabuterimon + Gryphonmon or Rosemon = Yanmamon

Digipedia

Every Digimon’s family tree, from Rookie to Mega. Tap a name to open its info card, which shows its type, specialty, weaknesses, moves and digivolutions.

  • Levels: a Digimon digivolves at EL 11 (Rookie to Champion), EL 21 (Champion to Ultimate) and EL 31 (Ultimate to Mega).
  • DP (Digivolve Points): where a tree branches, the game picks the branch whose DP badge matches your Digimon’s DP. “any DP” means there is only one branch. DP goes up by 1 each time you DNA Digivolve.
Stages, left to right as it grows: Rookie → Champion → Ultimate → Mega

DNA Chain

Finds the shortest chain of DNA Digivolves and level-ups from the Digimon you have to the one you want, with the moves you choose.

  1. Add the Digimon you have, with their DP. Max level and known moves are optional.
  2. Pick the Digimon you want and any moves it should end up with.
  3. Press Find shortest route. Each step shows what to combine or level up, and the DP and Max level that result.

Digimon you have

Must use in chain: tick this to make the route include that Digimon, for example to pass its moves down. Moves it knows: add moves a Digimon already has, so the route can count them. Max level: leave it blank if you don’t know it, and the route won’t limit that Digimon by level.

DigimonDPLevelMax levelMust use in chain

Digimon you want

Moves it should know by the end
Both parents pass every move they know to the DNA result. For each move, the route includes a Digimon that learns it and has it reach the learning level: EL 12 for a Champion move, EL 22 for Ultimate, EL 32 for Mega.

Rules the route follows

  • Shortest: the fewest DNA Digivolves first, then the fewest level-ups.
  • DP: a DNA result gets the higher parent’s DP + 1. Level-ups keep DP the same.
  • Max level: a DNA result’s Max level is the higher parent’s level + (the lower parent’s level ÷ 5), rounded down. The route assumes you train each parent to its Max level first.
  • Train to Max level: always level each Digimon to its Max level before you DNA Digivolve it. It ends up with better stats, and the result gets a higher Max level.
  • Level limits: a Digimon needs a Max level of at least 11, 21 or 31 to reach Champion, Ultimate or Mega. Max levels are only checked for Digimon you entered one for, and for lines made only from them.
  • Copies: unticked Digimon can be used more than once. When that happens, the route tells you how many extra to recruit. Ticked Digimon are used once.
  • No route: the route suggests wild Digimon to catch, Rookies first, then Champions. A Champion counts as two Rookie catches. It never suggests the Digimon you want or any Mega. Ultimates are only suggested if you allow them, and only when one saves at least five Rookie catches. Caught Digimon start at DP 0, and their Max level isn’t tracked.
DNA Level/Quality Calc

Plan a DNA Digivolve and see how strong the new Digimon will be.

  1. Parents (optional): enter both parents’ Level and Quality. You get the new Digimon’s Quality and Max level.
  2. New Digimon: check its Quality and Max level (filled in from step 1, or type them in yourself), then enter its starting stats.
  3. Result: its stats at Max level, next to what Quality 0, Quality 100 and the original game would give.

Starting stats are the numbers on its status screen at the start level. Growth is the species’ growth class for that stat (A grows best). Each new stage restarts the big early Attack and Defense gains, so the digivolve levels matter.

3Result

DNA rules

  • Max level = the higher parent’s level + (the lower parent’s level ÷ 5), rounded down. Which slot each parent is in doesn’t matter (tested in game). Example: EL 15 + EL 13 gives 15 + 2 = 17.
  • Quality comes from the higher-level parent. If both are the same level, the result gets the higher Quality. Example: EL 15 (Quality 66) + EL 12 (Quality 87) gives Quality 66.

How Quality changes growth

  • Better rolls: each level-up, every stat gains from one of 4 rolls, lowest to highest. At Quality 0 the chances are 50 / 30 / 15 / 5 %. At Quality 100 they are 5 / 15 / 30 / 50 %. Values in between scale evenly.
  • Bonus growth: every gain gets an extra Quality ÷ 10 %: +10 % at 100, +7.7 % at 77. Leftover fractions are saved and added in later.
  • Late levels: later in growth, Attack and Defense only rise on the best roll. Quality 0 gets it 5 % of the time and Quality 100 gets it 50 %, so high Quality keeps growing long after low Quality stops.
  • Not included: stat changes from digivolving itself, DNA, items and gear. Wild Digimon don’t show Quality; it’s set when one joins your party.

Digimon Moves

Every move a player Digimon can learn, with its stage, MP cost, power and side effects. Search for a move or a Digimon, filter by stage, kind or status, or tap a Digimon name in the table to see only its moves.

When moves are learned: each Digimon learns its move at EL 12 (Champion), EL 22 (Ultimate) or EL 32 (Mega). It keeps its moves when it digivolves, and DNA Digivolving passes both parents’ moves to the result.

Damage formula (approximate, because the game rounds the stats it shows):

damage = floor( floor(Type × Specialty × Power × MoveTile) × Attack ÷ floor(Defense × DefenderTile) )
  • Type: 1.2 if the attacker’s type beats the target’s, 0.8 if it loses, otherwise 1.0. Virus beats Data, Data beats Vaccine, Vaccine beats Virus.
  • Specialty: 1.2, 1.0 or 0.8, from the move’s element against the target’s specialty. For example, a Water move on a Fire Digimon is 1.2.
  • Power: the move’s listed power.
  • MoveTile: 1.2, 1.0 or 0.8, from the tile under the attacker against the move’s element. For example, a Darkness move used on a Darkness tile is 1.2.
  • Attack / Defense: the attacker’s Attack stat and the target’s Defense stat.
  • DefenderTile: 1.2, 1.0 or 0.8, from the tile under the target against the target’s own specialty.

Stat-down effects (Debuff moves that hit all enemies):

  • Duration: 3 rounds, not the whole battle.
  • No stacking: lowering a stat that’s already lowered only restarts the 3 rounds. For example, two Okuwamon using the same debuff have the same effect as one.
  • Bosses: take half the effect, and their stats never drop below 75% of the original value.
Boss and wild-only moves

No player Digimon learns these. Only bosses and wild Digimon use them, so they’re left out of the main list and the Weaknesses tab.

Power shows “–” for moves that don’t deal damage. Move data comes from a community skill list, and the effects are summarised in my own words.

How specialties work

Each arrow points from an element to the one it beats. A move does +20% (x1.2) against the element it beats and −20% (x0.8) against the element that beats it. Digimon and moves with no specialty always take and deal x1.0.

Type works the same way: Virus beats Data, Data beats Vaccine, Vaccine beats Virus. Specialty and type bonuses multiply, so the best case is x1.2 × x1.2 = x1.44.
